paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Peter shows up with a number, and Jesus answers with a story about a king and two debts. One debt is ten thousand talents. The other is a hundred denarii. Forgiving is never about counting, because the whole point is how much you were forgiven first (Matthew 18:22-24, 28).

Think about what the first servant had in his hands. He begged for patience, and the master gave him MORE than he asked for: compassion, a wiped-out debt, and a release (Matthew 18:26-27). And then he turned around and choked a man over a hundred denarii. I think he forgot where he'd been standing five minutes earlier, and friend, I've forgotten a lot of things, but I try not to forget that.

So the master asks the question that settles it: "Shouldn't you have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had on you?" (Matthew 18:33). Jesus closes by saying His heavenly Father will treat each of you that way unless you forgive your brother "from your heart" (Matthew 18:35). That means the forgiveness you've received is the reason you forgive, so go hand some out, baker. The teaching on humility and forgiveness ends here, and the Lord's mercy to you is what makes it possible.
